passages.text: When you sit down to dine with a ruler, consider carefully what is set before you, and put a knife to your throat if you possess a great appetite.
passages.sermon:
A ruler is a person who has authority and power.
When you sit down to eat with a ruler, pay close attention to what is in front of you.
Think carefully about the food that is offered to you.
If you have a strong desire for food, control yourself.
Be strict with yourself if you are tempted to eat too much.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תֵ֭שֵׁב לִלְח֣וֹם אֶת־ מוֹשֵׁ֑ל בִּ֥ין תָּ֝בִ֗ין אֶת־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃ וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ שַׂכִּ֣ין בְּלֹעֶ֑ךָ אִם־ בַּ֖עַל נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Do not crave his delicacies, for that food is deceptive.
passages.sermon: Do not desire his special foods.\r\nThat food is not honest.\r\nThat food deceives you.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּ֭תְאָו לְמַטְעַמּוֹתָ֑יו וְ֝ה֗וּא לֶ֣חֶם כְּזָבִֽים׃

passages.text: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; be wise enough to restrain yourself.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives advice about wealth.
It warns people not to exhaust themselves trying to become rich.
It tells people to stop and use wisdom.
It says, “Do not wear yourself out to get rich.”
It says, “Be wise enough to restrain yourself.”
passages.original: אַל־ תִּיגַ֥ע לְֽהַעֲשִׁ֑יר מִֽבִּינָתְךָ֥ חֲדָֽל׃

passages.text: When you glance at wealth, it disappears, for it makes wings for itself and flies like an eagle to the sky.
passages.sermon:
Wealth can vanish quickly.
If you look at wealth, it may be gone.
Wealth grows wings for itself.
Wealth flies away like an eagle in the sky.
passages.original: הֲתָעוּף עֵינֶ֥יךָ בּ֗וֹ וְֽאֵ֫ינֶ֥נּוּ כִּ֤י עָשֹׂ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה־ לּ֣וֹ כְנָפַ֑יִם כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר וְעָיֵף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃פ

passages.text: Do not eat the bread of a stingy man, and do not crave his delicacies; for he is keeping track, inwardly counting the cost. “Eat and drink,” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
passages.sermon:
A stingy man does not like to share.
He counts every cost in his mind.
Do not eat the bread of a stingy man.
Do not desire his special foods.
He may say, “Eat and drink.”
He does not mean it in his heart.
His heart is not with you.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּלְחַ֗ם אֶת־ לֶ֭חֶם רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְאַל־ תִּתְאָו לְמַטְעַמֹּתָֽיו׃ כִּ֤י׀ כְּמוֹ־ שָׁעַ֥ר בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ כֶּ֫ן־ ה֥וּא אֱכֹ֣ל וּ֭שְׁתֵה יֹ֣אמַר לָ֑ךְ וְ֝לִבּ֗וֹ בַּל־ עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: You will vomit up what little you have eaten and waste your pleasant words.
passages.sermon: You eat a small amount of food from a stingy man.\r\nYou will vomit it up.\r\nYou will waste your pleasant words.
passages.original: פִּֽתְּךָ־ אָכַ֥לְתָּ תְקִיאֶ֑נָּה וְ֝שִׁחַ֗תָּ דְּבָרֶ֥יךָ הַנְּעִימִֽים׃

passages.text: Do not speak to a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.
passages.sermon: A fool does not value wisdom.\r\nDo not speak to a fool.\r\nHe will despise the wisdom in your words.
passages.original: בְּאָזְנֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל אַל־ תְּדַבֵּ֑ר כִּֽי־ יָ֝ב֗וּז לְשֵׂ֣כֶל מִלֶּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless, for their Redeemer is strong; He will take up their case against you.
passages.sermon:
God cares for the fatherless.
Do not move an ancient boundary stone.
Do not enter the fields of orphans.
Their Redeemer is strong.
He will defend their cause against you.
passages.original: אַל־ תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם וּבִשְׂדֵ֥י יְ֝תוֹמִ֗ים אַל־ תָּבֹֽא׃ כִּֽי־ גֹאֲלָ֥ם חָזָ֑ק הֽוּא־ יָרִ֖יב אֶת־ רִיבָ֣ם אִתָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge.
passages.sermon:
You must seek wisdom.
You must open your heart to instruction.
You must listen carefully to words of knowledge.
You must pay attention with your ears.
You must desire to learn and understand.
passages.original: הָבִ֣יאָה לַמּוּסָ֣ר לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝אָזְנֶ֗ךָ לְאִמְרֵי־ דָֽעַת׃

passages.text: Do not withhold discipline from a child; although you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
passages.sermon:
A child needs discipline.
Do not keep discipline from a child.
If you strike a child with a rod, he will not die.
Discipline will not destroy him.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּמְנַ֣ע מִנַּ֣עַר מוּסָ֑ר כִּֽי־ תַכֶּ֥נּוּ בַ֝שֵּׁ֗בֶט לֹ֣א יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: Strike him with a rod, and you will deliver his soul from Sheol.
passages.sermon:
A father must discipline his child.
He must use the rod to correct him.
This discipline will save the child's soul from Sheol.
Sheol means the place of the dead.
Discipline protects the child from destruction.
passages.original: אַ֭תָּה בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט תַּכֶּ֑נּוּ וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מִשְּׁא֥וֹל תַּצִּֽיל׃

passages.text: My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will indeed rejoice.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
The father values wisdom.
He wants his son to have a wise heart.
If the son’s heart is wise, the father will rejoice.
The father’s own heart will be glad.
passages.original: בְּ֭נִי אִם־ חָכַ֣ם לִבֶּ֑ךָ יִשְׂמַ֖ח לִבִּ֣י גַם־ אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: My inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
passages.sermon:
I am a father who loves wisdom.
My deepest feelings will rejoice.
I will feel joy when you speak what is right.
Your lips must say honest and good words.
passages.original: וְתַעְלֹ֥זְנָה כִלְיוֹתָ֑י בְּדַבֵּ֥ר שְׂ֝פָתֶ֗יךָ מֵישָׁרִֽים׃

passages.text: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always continue in the fear of the LORD.
passages.sermon: Do not let your heart envy sinners.\r\nAlways fear the LORD.\r\nFear the LORD all day long.
passages.original: אַל־ יְקַנֵּ֣א לִ֭בְּךָ בַּֽחַטָּאִ֑ים כִּ֥י אִם־ בְּיִרְאַת־ יְ֝הוָ֗ה כָּל־ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
passages.sermon:
God promises a future to those who fear Him.
You have hope because God gives it.
Your hope will not end.
God will not let your hope be destroyed.
passages.original: כִּ֭י אִם־ יֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃

passages.text: Listen, my son, and be wise, and guide your heart on the right course.
passages.sermon:
My son, listen to me.
Become wise.
Guide your heart.
Choose the right path.
passages.original: שְׁמַע־ אַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֣י וַחֲכָ֑ם וְאַשֵּׁ֖ר בַּדֶּ֣רֶךְ לִבֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Do not join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat.
passages.sermon:
Do not join people who drink too much wine.
Do not join people who eat too much meat.
Avoid the company of drunkards.
Avoid the company of gluttons.
passages.original: אַל־ תְּהִ֥י בְסֹֽבְאֵי־ יָ֑יִן בְּזֹלֲלֵ֖י בָשָׂ֣ר לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: For the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe them in rags.
passages.sermon:
A drunkard wastes his life.
A glutton also wastes his life.
Both will become poor.
Drowsiness leads to poverty.
Drowsiness will make a person wear rags.
passages.original: כִּי־ סֹבֵ֣א וְ֭זוֹלֵל יִוָּרֵ֑שׁ וּ֝קְרָעִ֗ים תַּלְבִּ֥ישׁ נוּמָֽה׃

passages.text: Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
passages.sermon:
A father gives you life.
Listen to your father.
A mother grows old.
Do not despise your mother when she is old.
passages.original: שְׁמַ֣ע לְ֭אָבִיךָ זֶ֣ה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ וְאַל־ תָּ֝ב֗וּז כִּֽי־ זָקְנָ֥ה אִמֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Invest in truth and never sell it— in wisdom and instruction and understanding.
passages.sermon:
Seek truth.
Do not give up truth.
Value wisdom.
Value instruction.
Value understanding.
Hold on to these things.
Do not trade them away.
passages.original: אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל־ תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה׃

passages.text: The father of a righteous man will greatly rejoice, and he who fathers a wise son will delight in him.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man lives in a way that pleases God.
His father will rejoice greatly.
A wise son brings joy to his father.
The father delights in his wise son.
passages.original: גּוֹל יָגוֹל אֲבִ֣י צַדִּ֑יק יוֹלֵד חָ֝כָ֗ם וְיִשְׂמַח בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: May your father and mother be glad, and may she who gave you birth rejoice!
passages.sermon: A father can feel joy because of his child.\r\nA mother can feel joy because of her child.\r\nThe woman who gave birth to you can rejoice because of you.
passages.original: יִֽשְׂמַח־ אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.
passages.sermon: A father speaks to his son.\r\nHe asks his son to give him his heart.\r\nHe tells his son to let his eyes find joy in his ways.
passages.original: תְּנָֽה־ בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י וְ֝עֵינֶ֗יךָ דְּרָכַ֥י תִּרְצֶנָה׃

passages.text: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and an adulteress is a narrow well.
passages.sermon: A prostitute is a deep pit.\r\nAn adulteress is a narrow well.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲמֻקָּ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה וּבְאֵ֥ר צָ֝רָ֗ה נָכְרִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: Like a robber she lies in wait and multiplies the faithless among men.
passages.sermon:
A prostitute waits in secret like a robber.
She looks for people to deceive.
She causes more men to become unfaithful.
She increases the number of those who betray others.
passages.original: אַף־ הִ֭יא כְּחֶ֣תֶף תֶּֽאֱרֹ֑ב וּ֝בוֹגְדִ֗ים בְּאָדָ֥ם תּוֹסִֽף׃

passages.text: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaints? Who has needless wounds? Who has bloodshot eyes?
passages.sermon:
This passage asks important questions.
It asks about people who suffer.
It asks, "Who has woe?"
It asks, "Who has sorrow?"
It asks, "Who has arguments?"
It asks, "Who has complaints?"
It asks, "Who has wounds for no reason?"
It asks, "Who has red eyes?"
These questions describe people who experience pain and trouble.
passages.original: לְמִ֨י א֥וֹי לְמִ֪י אֲב֡וֹי לְמִ֤י מְדוֹנִים לְמִ֥י שִׂ֗יחַ לְ֭מִי פְּצָעִ֣ים חִנָּ֑ם לְ֝מִ֗י חַכְלִל֥וּת עֵינָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Those who linger over wine, who go to taste mixed drinks.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes people who spend much time with wine.
\r\nThese people stay long at their wine.
\r\nThey go to taste mixed drinks.
\r\nThey seek out strong drink.
\r\nThey desire to experience different kinds of alcohol.
passages.original: לַֽמְאַחֲרִ֥ים עַל־ הַיָּ֑יִן לַ֝בָּאִ֗ים לַחְקֹ֥ר מִמְסָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Do not gaze at wine while it is red, when it sparkles in the cup and goes down smoothly.
passages.sermon:
Wine can look beautiful.
Wine can appear red.
Wine can sparkle in the cup.
Wine can go down smoothly.
Do not stare at wine because of these things.
Do not let its appearance attract you.
passages.original: אַל־ תֵּ֥רֶא יַיִן֮ כִּ֪י יִתְאַ֫דָּ֥ם כִּֽי־ יִתֵּ֣ן בַּכִּיס עֵינ֑וֹ יִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃

passages.text: In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.
passages.sermon:
Wine can seem attractive and pleasant at first.
But in the end, wine harms you.
Wine bites like a snake.
Wine stings like a viper.
passages.original: אַ֭חֲרִיתוֹ כְּנָחָ֣שׁ יִשָּׁ֑ךְ וּֽכְצִפְעֹנִ֥י יַפְרִֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will utter perversities.
passages.sermon:
This passage warns about the effects of drinking wine.
Wine can lead to dangerous consequences.
If you drink too much wine, your eyes will see strange things.
You will see things that are not real.
Your mind will speak twisted words.
You will say things that are not right.
Drinking wine can confuse your thoughts.
It can make you speak in a wrong way.
passages.original: עֵ֭ינֶיךָ יִרְא֣וּ זָר֑וֹת וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ יְדַבֵּ֥ר תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת׃

passages.text: You will be like one sleeping on the high seas or lying on the top of a mast: “They struck me, but I feel no pain! They beat me, but I did not know it! When can I wake up to search for another drink?”
passages.sermon:
A person who drinks too much loses control.
He becomes confused and unaware.
He feels like someone lying in the middle of the sea.
He feels like someone lying on top of a ship’s mast.
People hit him, but he does not feel pain.
People beat him, but he does not know it happened.
He asks, “When will I wake up?”
He wants to find another drink.
passages.original: וְ֭הָיִיתָ כְּשֹׁכֵ֣ב בְּלֶב־ יָ֑ם וּ֝כְשֹׁכֵ֗ב בְּרֹ֣אשׁ חִבֵּֽל׃ הִכּ֥וּנִי בַל־ חָלִיתִי֮ הֲלָמ֗וּנִי בַּל־ יָ֫דָ֥עְתִּי מָתַ֥י אָקִ֑יץ א֝וֹסִ֗יף אֲבַקְשֶׁ֥נּוּ עֽוֹד׃
